answer: A proof-of-burn registry deters Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to permanently destroy scarce base tokens to anchor its identity on a shared ledger. An adversary incurs an irreversible capital cost per forged node, making mass identity generation economically prohibitive whether the agent buys industrial pigment or routes sensor data from a lagoon. However, this mechanism penalizes low-capital open-source agents and cannot stop well-funded attackers from subsidizing malicious swarms.
